subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: Should OpenClaw make reliable project/task memory a default core behavior, document it as a workspace/plugin pattern, or split this umbrella into narrower memory engine and session-recall fixes first?
rationale: Current main has partial primitives but no single established default contract for project/task state, and enabling broader recall has privacy and product-boundary tradeoffs that automation should not choose.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Tracks
options.body: Keep #48711 open as the broad reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

options.title: Route Recall To Existing Proposals
options.body: Use #99611 and #51386 as the primary cross-session recall product path while leaving this issue for project/task mutation semantics.

options.title: Document Workspace Pattern Only
options.body: Close the core default-behavior request if maintainers decide task memory should stay in a documented reliability pack or plugin rather than OpenClaw defaults.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep #48711 open as the broad reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The maintainer-authored #99611 proposal already frames the same-assistant recall product decision and privacy boundary most likely to decide this issue's cross-session scope.
